paper.title: Taming the Monster: A Fast and Simple Algorithm for Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: i.i.d. contextual bandit setting with a finite policy class (argmax-oracle access)
unmapped: Policy class Pi is accessed only via a cost-sensitive classification (argmax) oracle AMO
Context/reward-vector pairs drawn i.i.d. from a joint distribution D over X x [0,1]^A
settings.definition_quote: In the i.i.d.~contextual bandit setting, the context/reward vector pairs $(x_t,r_t) \in X \times [0,1]^A$ over all rounds $t = 1, 2, \dotsc$ are randomly drawn independently from $\D$. ... the (empirical cumulative) regret of the agent after $T$ rounds is defined as $\sum_{t=1}^T \bigl( r_t(\piopt(x_t)) - r_t(a_t) \bigr)$.

algorithms.name: ILOVETOCONBANDITS (Importance-weighted LOw-Variance Epoch-Timed Oracleized CONtextual BANDITS)

conditions: finite policy class Pi with |Pi| = N_exp

source.label: thm:regret-main
source.quote: Assume the optimization problem (\optprob) can be solved whenever required in Algorithm~\ref{alg:erucb}. With probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:erucb} (\ERUCB) after $T$ rounds is $O\left( \sqrt{KT\ln(T|\Pi|/\delta)} + K\ln(T|\Pi|/\delta) \right)$.

results.notes: Regret is empirical cumulative regret against the optimal policy pi_star (realized rewards), bounded w.p. 1-delta. Feasibility of (OP) is guaranteed by Theorem 3. Polynomial time given oracle access (oracle-efficient).

symbols.C_0: constant 4*psi + c_0 with psi=100, c_0 = 4*rho*(1+theta_1), theta_1=94.1, rho<=sqrt(2)
symbols.tau_mT: end round tau_{m(T)} of the epoch containing T

source.label: lem:regret
source.quote: For any $T \in \N$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret after $T$ rounds is at most $\biggerc \biggl( 4Kd_{\tau_{m_0-1}} + \sqrt{8Kd_{\tau_{m(T)}} \tau_{m(T)}} \biggr) + \sqrt{8T\log(2/\delta)}$ where $\biggerc := (4\vlc + \bigc)$ and $\bigc$ is defined in \lemref{inductive}.

results.notes: Explicit-constant version underlying Theorem 2; involves epoch-dependent quantities declared as symbols. Assumes (OP) solved each epoch.

tuning: doubling epoch schedule tau_m = 2^{m-1} or warm-start schedule

source.quote: There is an algorithm for the i.i.d.~contextual bandit problem with an optimal regret bound requiring $\tilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\frac{KT}{\ln(|\Pi|/\delta)}}\right)$ calls to the optimization oracle over $T$ rounds, with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

results.notes: Quantity is the total number of oracle (AMO) calls over T rounds, not regret; the accompanying regret is that of Theorem 2.

source.label: lem:doubling
source.quote: For the epoch schedule $\tau_m := 2^{m-1}$, the total number of calls to $\AMO$ is $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{KT/\logpd})$.

results.notes: Total number of AMO calls (computational guarantee); deterministic statement, 'expectation' chosen only as placeholder since no probability is stated.

tuning: epoch schedule (tau_1,tau_2)=(3,5), tau_m = m^2 for m>=3

source.label: lem:warm-start
source.quote: Define the epoch schedule $(\tau_1,\tau_2) := (3,5)$ and $\tau_m := m^2$ for $m \geq 3$ (this satisfies $\tau_{m+1} \leq 2\tau_m$). With high probability, the warm-start variant of \algref{erucb} makes $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{KT/\logpd})$ calls to $\AMO$ over $T$ rounds and $O(\sqrt{T})$ calls to \algref{coord}.

results.notes: Total oracle calls; also O(sqrt(T)) calls to the coordinate descent routine.

symbols.tau_M: round at end of epoch M in the epoch schedule

conditions: exists a distribution D and policy class Pi (constructed instance)

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: For any epoch schedule $0 = \tau_0 < \tau_1 < \tau_2 < \dotsb$ and any $M \in \N$ sufficiently large, there exists a distribution $\D$ over $X\times [0,1]^A$ and a policy class $\Pi$ such that, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $\inf_{m : \tau_m \geq \tau_M/2} \inf_{Q \in \lowvar{m}} |\supp(Q)| = \Omega\paren{ \sqrt{\frac{K\tau_M}{\ln(|\Pi|\tau_M/\delta)}} }$.

results.notes: Lower bound on support size of any distribution satisfying the low-variance constraint of (OP), hence on oracle calls for this class of optimization-based algorithms; not a regret bound.
